entries.originalText: “My Son, if thou set thy peace on any person because thou hast high opinion of him, and art familiar with him, thou shalt be unstable and entangled.
entries.modernizedText: “My Son, if you place your peace in any person because you think highly of him and are close to him, you will be unstable and entangled.

entries.originalText: But if thou betake thyself to the ever-living and abiding Truth, the desertion or death of a friend shall not make thee sad.
entries.modernizedText: But if you turn to the ever-living and abiding Truth, the desertion or death of a friend will not make you sad.

entries.originalText: In Me ought the love of thy friend to subsist, and for My sake is every one to be loved, whosoever he be, who appeareth to thee good, and is very dear to thee in this life.
entries.modernizedText: Your love for your friend ought to rest in Me, and for My sake you should love everyone, whoever he may be, who seems good to you and is very dear to you in this life.

entries.originalText: Without Me friendship hath no strength or endurance, neither is that love true and pure, which I unite not.
entries.modernizedText: Without Me friendship has no strength or endurance, nor is the love that I do not unite true and pure.

entries.originalText: Thou oughtest to be so dead to such affections of beloved friends, that as far as in thee lieth, thou wouldst rather choose to be without any companionship of men.
entries.modernizedText: You ought to be so dead to such affections for beloved friends that, as far as it lies in your power, you would rather choose to be without any human companionship.

entries.originalText: The nearer a man approacheth to God, the further he recedeth from all earthly solace.
entries.modernizedText: The nearer a person approaches God, the further he withdraws from all earthly comfort.

entries.originalText: The deeper also he descendeth into himself, and the viler he appeareth in his own eyes, the higher he ascendeth towards God.
entries.modernizedText: The deeper he descends into himself, and the more contemptible he appears in his own eyes, the higher he ascends toward God.

entries.originalText: “But he who attributeth anything good to himself, hindereth the grace of God from coming to him, because the grace of the Holy Ghost ever seeketh the humble heart.
entries.modernizedText: “But whoever attributes anything good to himself prevents the grace of God from coming to him, because the grace of the Holy Spirit always seeks the humble heart.

entries.originalText: If thou couldst make thyself utterly nothing, and empty thyself of the love of every creature, then should it be My part to overflow unto thee with great grace.
entries.modernizedText: If you could make yourself utterly nothing and empty yourself of love for every creature, then it would be My part to overflow upon you with great grace.

entries.originalText: When thou settest thine eyes upon creatures, the face of the Creator is withdrawn from thee.
entries.modernizedText: When you set your eyes on creatures, the face of the Creator is withdrawn from you.

entries.originalText: Learn in all things to conquer thyself for thy Creator’s sake, then shalt thou be able to attain unto divine knowledge.
entries.modernizedText: Learn to conquer yourself in all things for your Creator’s sake; then you will be able to attain divine knowledge.

entries.originalText: How small soever anything be, if it be loved and regarded inordinately, it holdeth us back from the highest good, and corrupteth.”
entries.modernizedText: However small a thing may be, if it is loved and regarded excessively, it holds us back from the highest good and corrupts us.”
